items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the poem 'For Anne Gregory', and answer.

"'Your voice,' said the boy, 'is so sweet that people will love you only for your songs.'
'Then I will sing no more,' said Mira,
'and speak in a plain, rough voice,
so that my friends may love me
for my heart and not my tune.'"

Answer the following:
(i) What does the boy say about Mira's voice?
(ii) What does Mira decide to do?  (a) Leave the town  (b) Become a teacher  (c) Sing louder  (d) Stop singing and speak in a plain voice
(iii) Which poem do these lines echo?  (a) "Amanda!"  (b) "Fog"  (c) "Fire and Ice"  (d) "For Anne Gregory"
(iv) What is common to Mira and Anne?
items.answer: (i) It is so sweet that people will love her only for her songs. (ii) (d) Stop singing and speak in a plain voice (iii) (d) "For Anne Gregory" (iv) Both want to be loved for their inner self, not an outer gift.
items.markingKey: (i) It is so sweet that people will love her only for her songs. (ii) (d) Stop singing and speak in a plain voice (iii) (d) "For Anne Gregory" (iv) Both want to be loved for their inner self, not an outer gift. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
